[34mInvestigated:[0m Grepped for `cleanDoubleSlashes` and `respectQueryAndFragment` across `src` and `README.md`. Read the trailing-slash helpers in `src/utils.ts`, the `cleanDoubleSlashes` implementation, its README entry, and the existing table-driven tests in `test/double-slash.test.ts`.

[33mLearned:[0m The trailing-slash helpers (`hasTrailingSlash`, `withoutTrailingSlash`, `withTrailingSlash`) already use a `respectQueryAndFragment` flag. Their opt-in branch splits off the fragment and query before editing the path. The original `cleanDoubleSlashes` splits on `://` and collapses slashes in every other segment, so query and hash text was affected.

[32mCompleted:[0m `cleanDoubleSlashes(input, respectQueryAndFragment?)` now accepts the flag. When true, only the portion before the first `?` or `#` is cleaned, so `/foo//bar?redirect=//baz` becomes `/foo/bar?redirect=//baz`. The default is unchanged. The old logic moved into a private helper, `_cleanDoubleSlashes`. JSDoc and the README entry were updated. New tests in `test/double-slash.test.ts` cover `?`, `#`, both together, full URLs with a protocol, input with no query or fragment, leading `?` or `#`, and a default-still-cleans check. The double-slash test file passes (13 of 13) and `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors. The full test suite was not run. Nothing has been committed.

[35mNext Steps:[0m No work is currently in progress. The session may receive further requests. Any follow-up would likely involve running the full test suite or committing the change.

[36mNotes:[0m The feature is scoped to the first `?` or `#`, so any `//` in the path after a query marker is also left alone. The full suite has not been run, so regressions outside the double-slash tests are unverified.
